==English==

===Pronunciation===
* {{IPA|en|/ʌnˈlaɪk/}}
* {{audio|en|en-us-unlike.ogg|a=US}}
* {{rhymes|en|aɪk|s=2}}

===Etymology 1===
From {{inh|en|enm|unlic}}, {{m|enm|unlich}}, from {{inh|en|ang|unlīċ}}, {{m|ang|unġelīċ|t=unlike, different, dissimilar, diverse}}, from {{inh|en|gem-pro|*ungalīkaz}}. {{surf|en|un-|like|id1=negative}}. Cognate with {{cog|nl|ongelijk}}, {{cog|de|ungleich}}, {{cog|non|úlíkr}} ''(see there for North Germanic descendants)''.

====Adjective====
{{en-adj}}

# Not like; [[dissimilar]] (to); having no resemblance; unalike.
#: {{ux|en|The brothers are quite '''unlike''' each other.}}
# [[unequal|Unequal]].
#: {{ux|en|They contributed in '''unlike''' amounts.}}
# {{lb|en|archaic}} Not likely; [[improbable]]; [[unlikely]].

=====Synonyms=====
* {{sense|not like}} See also [[Thesaurus:different]]

====Preposition====
{{en-head|prep}}

# Different from; not in a like or similar manner.
#: {{ux|en|The disgust I felt after watching last weekend's horror movie was '''unlike''' anything I had felt before.}}
# In contrast with; as opposed to.
#: {{ux|en|Claudia hardly ever drinks beer or wine, '''unlike''' Phillip, for whom the bar is practically a second home.}}
#* {{RQ:WaPo|date=February 10, 2009|page=C01|title=Signature Laps The Field With 39 Hayes Noms|author=Nelson Pressley|passage='''Unlike''' the elbows-out jostling in New York, there will be no campaigning:}}
#* {{RQ:Guardian|date=2024-06-20|author=Eva Corlett|title=Fidlets, fingies and riding a doo: study sheds light on Antarctic English slang|url=https://www.theguardian.com/world/article/2024/jun/20/fidlets-fingies-and-riding-a-doo-antarctica-english-slang-terms|passage=Antarctica, like outer-space, is known as an ICE environment – isolated, confined and extreme – meaning '''unlike''' other isolated communities, the rate of change for its vocabulary can be slower.|archiveurl=https://web.archive.org/web/20240809052943/https://www.theguardian.com/world/article/2024/jun/20/fidlets-fingies-and-riding-a-doo-antarctica-english-slang-terms}}
# Not typical of one's character or personality.
#: {{ux|en|Being late is '''unlike''' him.}}

====Noun====
{{en-noun}}

# Something that is not like something else; something different.

===Etymology 2===
From {{inh|en|enm|unliken}}, {{m|enm|unlyken}}, equivalent to {{pre|en|un|like|id1=reversive}}.

====Verb====
{{en-verb}}

# To [[dislike]].
# {{lb|en|social media}} To [[cancel]] a "[[like]]" action.
#: {{ux|en|I '''unliked''' the post after I found out the author was racist.}}
#* '''2009''', {{w|Ben Zimmer}}, “[http://www.nytimes.com/2009/09/20/magazine/20FOB-onlanguage-t.html On Language: The Age of Undoing]”, in ''The New York Times'' Magazine, 2009 September 20, page MM8:
## {{lb|en|by extension}} To [[withdraw]] support or enjoyment for.
##* {{quote-newsgroup|en|date=June 25 2010|author=TheKorn|url=http://groups.google.com/group/rec.games.pinball/msg/f8c07824c0044e93?q=unliking|title=Re: Pinball: RGP and/or Facebook|newsgroup=rec.games.pinball
|passage=My comment was more of a backhanded slap at Stern Pinball's Facebook "presence", specifically the garbage "cheap heat" posts. {{...}} It's so inane (and now, so constant) that I wound up "'''unliking'''" stern pinball entirely.}}

{{en-noun}}

# {{lb|en|internet}} The act of withdrawing one's [[like]] from a [[post]] on [[social media]].
#* {{quote-book|en|year=2012|author=Jesse Cannon; Todd Thomas|title=Get More Fans|page=552
|passage=Getting an '''unlike''' for every 20 likes is common and not something you need to be losing sleep over.}}
#* {{quote-book|en|year=2014|author=Ekaterina Walter; Jessica Gioglio|title=The Power of Visual Storytelling|page=13
|passage=On Facebook, users can also hide anyone in their network, including companies, from their News Feed, which is worse than an '''unlike''', as brands cannot measure how many people still like them but have hidden their status updates {{...}}}}
